video_title: Amazing Arizonans: Hall of famer Mike D'Antoni explains why coaching is harder than playing

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the difficulty of coaching versus playing basketball
quotes.excerpt: playing was much easier because once you finished, you could play well, you lose, you played well
quotes.quote: Playing was much easier because once you finished, you could play well, you lose, you played well, okay, so be it. You go home and you go the next day. But as a coach, it's only winning, winning and losing and somebody on the team is not playing well, that's your responsibility. So there's always something going on with the coach, it's much more difficult. But at the same time, when you do win, it is really rewarding. So a little love-hate relationship.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the emotional highs and lows of coaching
quotes.excerpt: I've never felt the excitement, the highs and the lows as a player, you feel highs and lows
quotes.quote: I've never felt the excitement, the highs and the lows as a player, you feel highs and lows, but not like as a coach. A coach is way up there over the top or you're on the couch in a fetal position getting beat to death.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on his transition from player to head coach in Italy
quotes.excerpt: I was lucky I played point guard the whole time, so you have to be an extension
quotes.quote: I was lucky I played point guard the whole time, so you have to be an extension of a coach anyway when you're playing that position. My father was a coach, my brother is a coach. I was extremely lucky to have the career that I did in Italy where I was able to start coaching as soon as I quit playing, they made me the head coach. I kind of learned a little bit by baptism, they threw me into the fire.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the collaborative nature of coaching success
quotes.excerpt: a coach is probably a product of his past experiences, good, bad, you learn from it
quotes.quote: I think a coach is probably a product of his past experiences, good, bad, you learn from it, you move forward. There's just so many people, Jerry Colangelo and Brian Colangelo, they gave me the opportunity to coach Phoenix. I was in Benetton and Gherardo Benetton, one of the classiest, nicest guys that owned the team, and I just keep on going. Dan Peterson was my coach in Milan for eight years, and he took me, I was coming out of the NBA, not having a great career, and I've lost my confidence as a player. So he took me, built me back up and made me as good as I could be as a basketball player.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the talented players he coached in Phoenix
quotes.excerpt: we got Steve Nash on, Marion, Amar'e Stoudemire, Joe Johnson, Quentin Richardson, then add Boris Diaw and Leandro Barbosa
quotes.quote: We got Steve Nash on, Marion, Amar'e Stoudemire, Joe Johnson, Quentin Richardson, then add Boris Diaw and Leandro Barbosa, Raja Bell, just so many good players that we had and it all fit. They were all good people, which for me is fundamental. The good teams I've had in Benetton or Milano or Phoenix, Houston, the bottom line is they're good people and they care and they work.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the importance of team culture and character
quotes.excerpt: it's a lot easier when you have people like the Colangelos and when Brian was picking the players
quotes.quote: It's a lot easier when you have people like the Colangelos and when Brian was picking the players or Jerry was building his organization, it was always first class and he made it seem like a family and you were invested. He's a pretty intimidating personality if you've been around him. So when he gives you that confidence or when they tap me as the head coach, confidence goes way up and you don't want to disappoint them.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the humor and personality of his former players
quotes.excerpt: Eddie House was one of the funniest guys I've ever been around. In Houston, I had this guy
quotes.quote: Eddie House was one of the funniest guys I've ever been around. In Houston, I had this guy, Corey Brewer is hilarious and he would come out right at the right time, he can mimic anybody, he would say things and just crack up everybody. But yeah, Eddie House was a good one. A lot of guys were funny, didn't mean to be.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the unique team chemistry of his Phoenix squad
quotes.excerpt: we're on a bus in Toronto, it's about 2:00 in the morning, they're playing the Temptations
quotes.quote: We're on a bus in Toronto, it's about 2:00 in the morning, they're playing the Temptations, they're playing Motown songs. They're all starting to sing. They're all back here singing, thank God for Walter McCarty who's the only one that could sing. So he's like belting it out and it's just, you know, the bus driver turned to me and he goes, you know, I've been driving teams for 30 years, I've never ever heard this happen to a team. And it's just those are the moments you cherish.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on his coaching philosophy regarding player success
quotes.excerpt: I wanted each player to have a career year and to get paid, because that's what ultimately
quotes.quote: I wanted each player to have a career year and to get paid, because that's what ultimately they're there for. I want their families to be taken care of and they're taken care of. Now, yeah, they make a lot of money, but sometimes that's got to last from age 35 until until they die, 70, 75, 80, 90, and they got to take care of the families. A lot of them were taking care of cousins and uncles and different things, mothers and dads. And so I wanted them to be financially okay.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on coaching Shaquille O'Neal in Phoenix
quotes.excerpt: Shaq, you know, being in Phoenix had one half a year for me and then I think
quotes.quote: Shaq, you know, being in Phoenix had one half a year for me and then I think, you know, he was there maybe a year and a half. But he was one of the funniest and good guys to coach that I've ever been around. He was very coachable, wanted to learn our system. He didn't want us, because he is a system, like James Harden said, you know, hey, I don't fit into a system, I am the system and he's right. Those guys are that good where they are, but he wanted to fit in with everybody and just kept the locker room in hysterics.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the post-career success of his former players
quotes.excerpt: Boris Diaw is head of the French Federation for basketball, so he's head of their Olympic team
quotes.quote: Boris Diaw is head of the French Federation for basketball, so he's head of their Olympic team and everything. So many people go on to do some great things, it's great.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the evolution of player skills in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: before you wouldn't have seven-footers shooting threes. You know, now you got them all over the place
quotes.quote: Before you wouldn't have seven-footers shooting threes. You know, now you got them all over the place. You'd have one or two, you know, like Bob McAdoo, 6'11, and he was back in the 80s, he could shoot out there or Dirk Nowitzki. So, but now there's a lot of them doing it. And then you got Wemby, who at 7'4 can do things that you can only, you can't believe what he's doing.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the 2004 rule changes and Phoenix's success
quotes.excerpt: the rules changed the 2004 when Steve Nash came to Phoenix and we were all able to
quotes.quote: The rules changed the 2004 when Steve Nash came to Phoenix and we were all able to open it up, freedom of movement, and we took advantage of a rule change. So a little bit of luck went involved in also our success.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on James Harden's mastery of the game
quotes.excerpt: his mastery of the game was ridiculous. How what he could do and manipulate the referees
quotes.quote: His mastery of the game was ridiculous. How what he could do and manipulate the referees, manipulate the game and get 50 points, didn't seem anything to him.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the herd mentality in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: the league is a bunch of sheep, they all follow together. They all, they don't want to
quotes.quote: The league is a bunch of sheep, they all follow together. They all, they don't want to get out there and, you know, take the first one through the door because they could be the one, you know, taking the bullets.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on his coaching philosophy regarding on-court intensity
quotes.excerpt: once you're inside the lines on court, it's the most important thing in the world
quotes.quote: Once you're inside the lines on court, it's the most important thing in the world. Once you're outside, it's the least important thing in the world where you got your family, you got friends, you got to take care of and you got and be nice, be a a citizen. And but when you're on the court, yeah, we compete, but when you're over, it's over.
